text:
jamie (support): FYI we got a SEV from a customer in eu-west-1 — embed endpoint p95 jumped ~3x around 08:12UTC. They say it started after a maintenance window last night. Request id sample: r-0a1b2c3d.

maya (eng-runtime): thanks, collecting traces now. which model & route?

jamie (support): model: text-embed-512-v1, route: /v1/embeddings (customer uses batch size 8). Happened across multiple instances. Customer attached curl repro.

oliver (eng-infra): I see a driver blob update rolled to eu-west-1 at 02:10 UTC — kernel+nvme driver package. Rolling out to remaining hosts is paused.

liz (sre-oncall): can we get a p95 metric graph for that timeframe (30m window) and host-level disk IO? I want tail latency and queue depth. @deploy-bot can you snapshot topo and inflight request counts for the cluster? :eyes:

deploy-bot: snapshot created: snap-1719992222-01 (hosts: euw-ml-10..18) — queued-reqs: [2,3,1,4,0,7,5,2,1]

maya (eng-runtime): looking at traces for r-0a1b2c3d — majority of added latency (~120ms) is in model shard fetch + disk wait on hostfs read (nvme). KV cache hits unchanged.

oliver (eng-infra): that matches io stats — host euw-ml-14 shows sustained nvme avg lat 3.2ms and p95 ~18ms during spike. other hosts ~0.8ms. Pattern started right after node went through the driver package update.

jamie (support): customer says they rerouted small traffic to us-west and p95 dropped back to normal. Could we route them away from eu-west as a mitigation?

liz (sre-oncall): short-term mitigation options: 1) route traffic to other region (support can coordinate) 2) cordon affected hosts and drain 3) roll back driver package on those hosts. Which is fastest?

oliver (eng-infra): fastest is cordon+drain for euw-ml-14 and euw-ml-15, then failover. Rollback needs image build and validation — estimate 45-60m.

maya (eng-runtime): also we can temporarily lower batch size via per-customer routing policy (reduce to 4) to lower IO pressure while infra works on hosts. Jamie can we ask customer permission?

jamie (support): on it. asking for permission to reduce batch to 4 and to shift 30% of traffic to us-west. will update in 5m. :phone:

oliver (eng-infra): starting live host checks: running iostat & nvme-cli smart-log on euw-ml-14. If SMART shows errors, we'll mark for disk replacement.

maya (eng-runtime): repro snippet from customer (they sent):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-512-v1","input":["...","...","..."]}'
```
We also asked for a full HAR + server request id mapping.

deploy-bot: host euw-ml-14: nvme smart-health: 0 warnings, media_errors: 0; iostat: avg await 3.1ms, util 92% during window.

oliver (eng-infra): weird — smart looks fine but util high. suspect driver change altered qdepth or IO scheduler defaults. I'll diff kernel params between euw-ml-14 and a healthy host.

maya (eng-runtime): meanwhile I toggled per-route batch override for this customer to size=4 and max_concurrency=2 for the eu-west routing policy. Will monitor.

jamie (support): customer approved batch reduction + partial traffic shift. They've routed 30% to us-west now. Confirmed their p95 dropped ~40% after shift. :+1:

liz (sre-oncall): good. infra please run a bisect plan: pick a healthy host, replicate driver package, boot in staging, run the same disk-heavy embed workload to reproduce. If repro, gather perf counters (io_uring, block layer qdepth, scheduler) and open kernel bug report.

oliver (eng-infra): starting staging repro with driver package from 02:10 image. Running 30m soak with batch=8 to reproduce. I'll attach perf logs here when done.

maya (eng-runtime): add a runtime metric: host fs read p99 latency per-request (already added). If downstream shows sustained high p99 we can auto-failover those hosts.

jamie (support): customer is happy with the temporary measures. They asked for ETA on full fix. Suggested ETA: infra will either rollback or patch QOS within 2-4 hours.

oliver (eng-infra): if staging repros we will prepare rollback image and schedule rolling rollback to affected hosts. ETA 2 hours if repro confirmed, 4 hours if root cause needs kernel driver patch.

liz (sre-oncall): updating incident timeline and severity to S2. Keep thread updated whenever we see repro or rollback start.

maya (eng-runtime): quick note: I added a tracing span to mark fs-read wait to help correlate from traces — should make postmortem clearer.

deploy-bot: staging run complete: reproduced p95 increase on driver image. Collected perf artifacts: perf-1719992400.tar.gz (uploading to /artifacts).

oliver (eng-infra): confirmed repro. diff shows driver changed default IO scheduler tunables and max_hw_queues. Opening GH issue to track rollback + vendor escalation.

jamie (support): relaying to customer — rollback planned now, rolling out to affected hosts. Expect next status in ~30m. Thanks all.

maya (eng-runtime): once rollback is live i'll run a few canary requests and report p95.

liz (sre-oncall): thanks team. postmortem action items: add pre-merge perf test for driver package, add automated host-level nvme util alarms, and add routing playbook for region failover.

jamie (support): incident note: customer impact minimized by batching change + partial region shift. Will follow up with a postmortem and the artifacts. :memo:
